title: Search - Pill
description: Rounded pill wrapper for the Blog All Articles search box, no-button — a leading magnifying-glass icon replaces the submit button (a real accessibility win, not just a style choice). This is a plain core/search form: submitting it navigates to the site's global search results, it does not filter the All Articles grid in place — core has no mechanism to bind core/search to a specific nested Query Loop, even with enhancedPagination (confirmed against core's own render/Interactivity code). Accepted for now; revisit once ls-plugin/taxonomy-filter (or an equivalent) supports search-term filtering the same way it already supports category filtering. Only overrides what `styles/presets/blocks/core-search.json` (the site-wide core/search default) doesn't already set. With no button, core/search renders the input directly on the block root (no `.wp-block-search__inside-wrapper`). core/search's own `selectors.border` maps a JSON `border` key to `.wp-block-search__input`, not the root — but the input also needs `border:none`/`background:transparent` so it doesn't draw a second box inside the pill, which silently cancelled out a JSON-key border entirely. Border, radius, and background are therefore all authored directly on the root (`&`) in the `css` field instead, so they can't be reset by the input override. The icon glyph has no block-supports equivalent — no icon slot exists on core/search — so it's a mask-image data URI tinted via text.muted, the same JSON-limitation class as other pseudo-element glyphs in this theme. Border uses the border.field token (neutral-600, both modes) rather than border.card (neutral-300/800) — this border is the pill's only visible field boundary, and border.card only reaches ~1.3:1 against the card surface, well under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text minimum; border.field is verified at 4.5:1 light / 3.59:1 dark.
